newsitem.title: UK: Whitbread not seen taking Welcome Break.
newsitem.headline: Whitbread not seen taking Welcome Break.

text.p: Brewing-to-leisure group Whitbread Plc on Monday was seen as a non-runner in the 370 million stg contest for the Welcome Break British motorway service areas which Granada Group Plc is selling.
Whitbread was named by newspapers as one of six groups on Granada's short-list to buy the Welcome Breaks but industry sources said Whitbread had withdrawn from the battle.

Granada is disposing of some 21 UK service areas, which it acquired as part of its acquisition of Forte a year ago. The deal gave Granada a near-monopoly on the motorways and the sale is part of an agreement with the UK competition authorities.
Whitbread had agreed to buy the Welcome Breaks, along with the Little Chef roadside restaurants, from Forte for 1.05 billion stg in the event of the Granada bid lapsing.
The sources said Whitbread was believed to regard the Welcome Break as the least attractive part of the package it had sought to buy from Forte.
Coach operator National Express was also named as a candidate to acquire the service areas, which are likely to raise some 370 million stg and and are expected to be sold in the next 10 weeks or so.

National Express declined to comment. However, analysts noted that the company had recently expanded its operations and now owns and manages two English airports and a number of bus and rail stations.
Granada said there had been a good level of interest in the service areas but would not comment on the main bidders.
National Express shares were up 1.5p at 544p on Monday, having earlier hit a record high of 546p. The recent rise has been helped by a stock shortage.
Granada was 12.5p higher at 854.5p, while Whitbread had gained 3p to 764.5p.
